fr:title.text: Why zsh startup is slow on macproseph

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Why zsh startup is slow on macproseph

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Analysis of ~/nix-config/home.nix (the programs.zsh block and its initContent). The config layers several frameworks and eval-at-startup integrations; each one adds fixed cost to every new shell.

oh-my-zsh + zplug loaded together. Both frameworks are enabled (programs.zsh.oh-my-zsh.enable = true and programs.zsh.zplug.enable = true). Even with only the git plugin, oh-my-zsh sources its full library (lib/*.zsh), scans for updates, and runs compinit. Pure is loaded via zplug, so oh-my-zsh's theme machinery is pure overhead — ZSH_THEME="" is set but the framework still loads.

zsh-vi-mode plugin. Known to add ~50–150ms on its own because it rebinds the full keymap at init. The defer:2 zplug tag helps by running it after the first prompt, but the parsing cost still lands on startup.
Multiple eval "$(...)" subprocess inits. Each of these forks a process and sources its output on every shell start:

html:ul.html:li: eval "$(any-nix-shell zsh)" — wraps nix-shell/nix develop and installs precmd hooks
eval "$(zoxide init zsh --cmd cd)" — replaces cd
programs.fzf.enableZshIntegration — sources key bindings and completion

fr:mainmatter.html:p: enableCompletion = true runs compinit on every start. With many packages in $fpath (Nix profile, Homebrew, Cargo, etc.) this is one of the single largest costs in a default zsh setup. There is no zcompdump reuse config visible.
autosuggestion and syntaxHighlighting each source a few hundred lines of zsh at startup and install widget hooks. Individually small, together ~20–40ms.

html:ul.html:li: ulimit -n 10240 — negligible, but it runs in both .bashrc and the zsh initContent.
The claude and emacs-ensure-daemon shell functions — trivial, just function definitions.
Many shellAliases — parsed quickly, not a real factor.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Before changing anything, profile to see where the time actually goes:

html:ul.html:li: Coarse: for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do /usr/bin/time zsh -i -c exit; done
Per-line trace: start zsh with zsh -xvi 2>/tmp/zsh.trace -c exit and inspect slow sections.
zprof: add zmodload zsh/zprof at the top of initContent and zprof at the bottom; the next interactive shell prints a per-function timing table.

html:ol.html:li: Drop oh-my-zsh. Pure + zplug already cover the prompt and plugin loading. Keep the git aliases you actually use by copying them into shellAliases.
Lazy-load or remove zsh-vi-mode if you rarely use vi keybindings. If you want to keep it, confirm defer:2 is actually deferring (it only works if zplug's zplug load happens after precmd).
Cache compinit. Gate it to run at most once a day: autoload -Uz compinit; compinit -C (or check zcompdump mtime). Home-manager's enableCompletion doesn't do this by default.
Replace eval "$(... init zsh)" with static snippets. zoxide init zsh output is stable; capture it once into a file and source it to skip the subprocess fork. Same for any-nix-shell if you keep it.
Consider dropping any-nix-shell — you already use direnv + nix-direnv for per-project shells, so the interactive nix-shell wrapper may be unused.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: None of this is destructive; do the profiling first so you can attribute savings to each change.

Profiled with zprof. Actual breakdown (total ~2870ms): __zplug::log::write::info 1506ms (52%), __zplug::core::cache::diff 434ms (15%), compdump + compinit combined ~515ms (18%). Pure, zsh-async, vi-mode (with defer:2), syntax-highlighting, autosuggestions — all effectively free. The original guesses about oh-my-zsh and vi-mode were wrong; zplug's own cache/log machinery dominated.

html:ol.html:li: Removed the empty oh-my-zsh block (unused; prompt comes from Pure).
Dropped programs.zsh.zplug entirely. Replaced with programs.zsh.plugins = [ zsh-vi-mode ] (home-manager sources it directly, no framework).
Added pkgs.pure-prompt to home.packages; wired up prompt with autoload -U promptinit then promptinit; prompt pure.
Added completionInit override that uses compinit -C when ~/.zcompdump is less than 24h old, full rebuild otherwise.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Outcome: the user reports "much faster" startup on a fresh shell — qualitative confirmation; no post-change zprof number captured.
